issues.t: Retractable hardtop stops partway or won't move
issues.sym: The power hardtop stalls halfway, won't start to open or close, or you hear the pump running while the roof doesn't move. The trunk may open but the roof never follows.
issues.why: The roof relies on several position sensors, a control module and a hydraulic pump. A sensor that reads wrong, low hydraulic fluid or a leaking cylinder stops the sequence as a safety measure.
issues.next: Don't force the roof by hand. Check that the trunk is fully closed and the cargo divider is in place, then have a shop that knows XLRs scan the roof module and check sensor readings and pump fluid.

issues.t: Roof panel separates from the frame
issues.sym: The front roof panel lifts, flutters or comes completely off the frame, usually at highway speed.
issues.why: The outer roof skin is bonded to its frame with adhesive. On some cars the bond lets go over time. GM collected field data on this roof skin separation in 2019.
issues.next: If you see a gap at the roof edge, a lifting skin or hear wind noise from the top, stop driving at speed and have the bond inspected right away. A loose panel can strike cars behind you.

issues.t: Hydraulic fluid leak from the roof cylinders or lines
issues.sym: Oily fluid in the trunk or roof storage area, and the roof moves slowly or stops working.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for fluid seeping from the roof's hydraulic cylinders and for roof hydraulic lines that rub through at the right rear.
issues.next: Have the cylinders and lines checked for wetness. Fixing a leak early saves the pump from running dry.

issues.t: Gasoline smell or fuel leak from the tank lines
issues.sym: Strong raw-gas smell around the car or in the garage, wet spots under the rear, or a check engine light for an evaporative leak.
issues.why: The XLR uses two linked fuel tanks. Owners report leaks at the crossover pipe, the feed lines and the pump connection, and GM ran a service campaign for leaks at the tank's quick connectors.
issues.next: Treat any fuel smell as urgent: park outside and have the tank lines inspected. Ask a Cadillac dealer with your VIN whether the quick-connector campaign was done.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or drops to empty
issues.sym: The fuel gauge jumps around, reads half full after you fill up, or reads empty with fuel still in the tank. Some cars can run out of fuel with the gauge near half.
issues.why: The fuel level sensors in the twin tanks give bad readings. GM put out bulletins and revised sender values for the Corvette and XLR.
issues.next: Track miles since your last fill-up until it is fixed. A shop can check the sender readings and update or replace the level sensor.

issues.t: Engine oil leaks from the Northstar V8
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell after driving, or oil wetness at the front or bottom of the engine.
issues.why: The Northstar V8 is known for seeping at the lower crankcase seal, oil pan gasket and front cover. GM issued several bulletins for oil leaks at the front, rear and crankcase on the XLR engine.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the leak traced. Small seeps can be watched, but leaks onto the exhaust are a fire risk and should be fixed.

issues.t: Shift cable breaks so the car won't shift or stays in gear
issues.sym: The shifter moves but the car stays in Park, or it moves in a different gear than the shifter shows. Some owners had the car roll or move in reverse unexpectedly.
issues.why: The cable that connects the shifter to the rear-mounted transmission can fray and snap with age.
issues.next: Stop driving and set the parking brake if the shifter feels loose or the gear doesn't match. Have the shift cable replaced before using the car.

issues.t: Shifter won't come out of Park at times
issues.sym: You press the brake but the shift lever stays locked in Park.
issues.why: GM published a bulletin for XLRs whose shift lever could not be moved out of Park at times.
issues.next: Check that the brake lights work, since the shift lock uses the brake switch. A dealer can check the shift lock parts and any bulletin repair.

issues.t: Headlights or running lights melt, fog up or fail
issues.sym: Headlight or daytime running light lenses look melted, cloudy or full of moisture, or lamps stop working.
issues.why: Heat and water get into the lamp housings. GM issued bulletins for water in the headlamps, and owners report melted running light lenses. New replacement lamps are hard to find now.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have the lamps checked before an inspection. Used or rebuilt assemblies are often the only option, so shop around.

issues.t: Turn signal and running light bulb burns out early (recall)
issues.sym: The turn signal indicator on the dash flashes faster than normal, or the front turn signal or running light is out.
issues.why: One bulb does the job of running light, turn signal and parking lamp. A loose socket or a poor seal makes it burn out early.
issues.next: Ask a Cadillac dealer to check your VIN for recall 06V263000. They replace both sockets and bulbs for free.

issues.t: Rear brake lines can overheat from the exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, longer stops, or brake fluid leaking at the rear.
issues.why: The rear brake lines can sit too close to the left exhaust and get hot enough to boil the brake fluid or wear through.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Have a dealer confirm recall 04V525000 was done. They check clearance, reroute the lines and replace any that are worn.

issues.t: Lower control arm ball joint nut can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk from a corner of the car, the car pulling to one side, or a wheel tilted outward.
issues.why: The washer under the ball joint nut was made of the wrong steel and can crack, so the nut loses clamp and the control arm can separate from the knuckle.
issues.next: Make sure recall 04V273000 was done. If you hear clunks, stop and have the suspension checked.

issues.t: Engine may not return to idle in extreme cold (recall)
issues.sym: In very cold weather the engine may be slow to drop back to idle after you lift off the gas, so stopping takes more brake effort.
issues.why: The accelerator pedal has two return springs. If one breaks at about -22°F or colder, the pedal may not return quickly enough to meet the federal standard.
issues.next: Check that recall 05V046000 was done. The dealer replaces the accelerator pedal assembly.

issues.t: Cracked or broken composite leaf spring
issues.sym: A clunk or bang over bumps, the car sitting lower on one corner or end, or harsh, uneven ride.
issues.why: Like the Corvette, the XLR uses plastic composite leaf springs across the car. GM issued a bulletin for front and rear composite springs that crack or break on 2004–2009 XLRs.
issues.next: Have the springs inspected on a lift. A broken spring changes ride height and handling, so replace it before driving hard.

issues.t: Leaking shocks or 'Service Suspension' warning
issues.sym: A 'Service Suspension System' message, a bouncy or harsh ride, or oil wetness on a shock.
issues.why: The Magnetic Ride shocks can leak with age, and GM issued a bulletin for the shock wiring connectors not being fully seated.
issues.next: Have the suspension codes read and the connectors checked first, since that is the simpler fix. Confirm a leak before replacing a magnetic shock.

issues.t: StabiliTrak brakes a wheel or the rear steps out unexpectedly
issues.sym: The stability control kicks in on its own, one wheel brakes, the rear of the car slides, or you see 'Service StabiliTrak' messages.
issues.why: Owners report the stability system acting without a reason, which points to a faulty wheel speed, steering angle or yaw sensor, or a wiring fault.
issues.next: Have the stability and ABS codes read and the sensors tested. Drive gently until it is diagnosed, especially in the wet.

issues.t: Brake rotor surface cracks
issues.sym: Fine cracks on the rotor faces, brake noise or a pulsing pedal.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin, shared with the Corvette, covering rotor surface cracking from heat cycles on 2005–2009 cars.
issues.next: Have the rotors inspected at each brake service. Small surface checks are often normal, but deep cracks mean the rotor should be replaced.

issues.t: Front brakes squeal under light braking
issues.sym: A squeal from the front when you press the brake pedal lightly.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for front brake squeal on the XLR during normal stops.
issues.next: A shop can install updated pads or anti-noise parts. The noise alone is not a safety issue if the pads have plenty of material.

issues.t: Run-flat tires wear fast or bubble
issues.sym: A bulge in the tire sidewall, fast wear, or a flat with no spare tire in the car. Replacement tires can take days to arrive.
issues.why: The XLR comes with run-flat tires and no spare. Their stiff sidewalls can bubble after a pothole.
issues.next: Check tire pressure monthly and inspect sidewalls after hard hits. A sidewall bubble means the tire must be replaced.

issues.t: Doors won't open with a dead battery or failed fob
issues.sym: The electronic door buttons don't open the doors, or you can get stuck inside or outside the car when the battery is weak.
issues.why: The XLR uses electric door releases instead of normal handles. GM sent an advisory about the inside manual release for when the battery is low or the fob doesn't work.
issues.next: Learn where the manual inside release is from your owner's manual. Replace a weak battery early and keep a spare fob battery.

issues.t: Driver door won't open from the outside touch pad
issues.sym: The driver's door opens from inside but not from the outside touch pad.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for the driver door touch pad not working from outside.
issues.next: A dealer can check the touch pad switch and door module. Use the key fob or the inside release meanwhile.

issues.t: No start from steering column lock fault
issues.sym: The car won't start, or you get a steering column message, and the steering wheel may stay locked.
issues.why: The electric steering column lock module can lose communication with the car, and GM issued a bulletin on this.
issues.next: Have the column lock module codes read. Don't keep cranking; a dealer or specialist can test the module and wiring.

issues.t: Water in the trunk or passenger footwell
issues.sym: Wet carpet in the passenger footwell, water in the trunk well behind the roof, or electrical glitches after rain.
issues.why: Roof drains can clog, letting water collect. GM also issued a bulletin on water leaking at the passenger floor near the body control module.
issues.next: Check and clear the roof drains, especially the one by the driver-side trunk opening. Dry the carpet quickly so the module and wiring aren't damaged.

issues.t: Ratcheting or clicking noise on cold start
issues.sym: A brief ratcheting or clicking sound from the engine right after a cold start.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for this cold-start noise on the 4.6L Northstar.
issues.next: If it goes away in seconds, it is usually harmless, but mention it at service so the dealer can check the bulletin.

issues.t: Blue smoke at startup
issues.sym: A puff of blue smoke from the exhaust right after starting, then it clears.
issues.why: Oil seeps past the valve seals or rings while the car sits. GM issued a bulletin for this on the 4.6L Northstar in the XLR.
issues.next: Watch your oil level. If smoke is heavy or the engine uses more than a quart every couple thousand miles, have it checked.

issues.t: Rear axle chatter or clunk on turns
issues.sym: A chatter, shudder or clunk from the rear when turning slowly, such as in parking lots.
issues.why: The rear differential fluid breaks down. GM's bulletin calls for draining and refilling the differential with the correct fluid and additive.
issues.next: Have the rear differential fluid changed. This usually stops the chatter.

issues.t: Telescoping steering wheel won't adjust
issues.sym: The power tilt or telescope steering column doesn't move when you use the switch.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for the XLR telescoping steering wheel not working.
issues.next: Have the column motor and switch checked. It's a comfort issue, not a safety one.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leak at the pump hose
issues.sym: Power steering fluid dripping near the front of the engine, whining when turning, or a low fluid level.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for leaks at the high-pressure hose connection to the power steering pump.
issues.next: Keep the reservoir topped up and have the hose connection resealed or the hose replaced.
